text:
Utah and Pittsburgh both arrive 2-3-0 in their last five, and they've already traded blows this month: the Mammoth won 5-4 on Oct 19, a game our numbers say they deserved to win 75% of the time (the share of simulated replays of every shot that they win). Utah lost 3-1 to Minnesota two days ago and is without John Marino and Michael Carcone. Pittsburgh, rested after four days off, is thin up front: Bryan Rust is on injured reserve, and Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell, up to 18:04 a night from 14:05. Evgeni Malkin is day-to-day and could return.

The teams are close on chances. At five on five, Utah has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of shots taken and allowed) and Pittsburgh 54%. Utah's penalty trouble, 4.7 minors a game, keeps feeding power plays. The goalies, both projected, are Karel Vejmelka and Arturs Silovs. Vejmelka sits 3.96 goals worse than expected this season (5.6 worse over his last five starts), though he was 5.39 better last year. Silovs is 1.47 better than expected this year after finishing 12.76 below last season.

We'd watch Dylan Guenther, who we have at 37% to score and who struck on the power play Saturday, and Rakell at 30% for Pittsburgh. As Yahoo Sports put it, "The Penguins saw the old Rickard Rakell on Saturday. They need that guy back." Our under-the-radar pick is Utah's Anders Lee: he plays about 13 minutes on the third line, but he has 3.8 expected goals in his last 10 games, and we have him at 22% to score.
